Calculate a composite schedule advantage

Source: R/schedule_advantage.R
calculate_schedule_advantage.Rd

Combines rest disparity, travel disparity, and body-clock disparity into a single pre-game score. Positive schedule_advantage favors the home team. The raw parts and their point values are kept in the output so the weighting can be checked or changed.

Usage

calculate_schedule_advantage(
  schedule,
  team_home = nfl_airports,
  venues = nfl_stadiums,
  trip_model = c("itinerary", "round_trip"),
  points_per_rest_day = 0.25,
  points_per_1000_travel_miles = 0.5,
  points_per_tz_hour = 0.35,
  east_weight = 1,
  west_weight = 0.5
)

Arguments

schedule

A data frame accepted by calculate_rest_disparity(), calculate_travel_miles(), and flag_time_zone_shifts(). It needs game_id, gameday, home_team, and away_team; gametime, stadium_id, and location improve accuracy when present.

team_home

Team home-base lookup. Defaults to nfl_airports.

venues

Venue lookup. Defaults to nfl_stadiums.

trip_model

Travel model passed to calculate_travel_miles(). Defaults to "itinerary".

points_per_rest_day

Points per day of rest disparity. Defaults to 0.25.

points_per_1000_travel_miles

Points per 1,000 miles of extra travel. Defaults to 0.5.

points_per_tz_hour

Points per hour of body-clock penalty disparity. Defaults to 0.35.

east_weight, west_weight

Multipliers for eastward and westward clock shifts passed to flag_time_zone_shifts(). Defaults are 1 and 0.5.

Value

schedule with the rest columns from calculate_rest_disparity(), plus home_trip_miles, away_trip_miles, travel_disparity, home_tz_shift_hours, away_tz_shift_hours, home_body_clock_penalty, away_body_clock_penalty, tz_penalty_disparity, rest_points, travel_points, time_zone_points, schedule_advantage, components_missing, and advantage_category.

Details

The default score is 0.25 * rest_disparity + 0.5 * travel_disparity / 1000 + 0.35 * tz_penalty_disparity, where travel_disparity = away_trip_miles - home_trip_miles and tz_penalty_disparity = away_body_clock_penalty - home_body_clock_penalty. A missing component (for example, rest in a season opener) contributes zero and increments components_missing; the raw component columns keep the NA so the omission is visible. The default weights are a starting point, not fitted values. Use eval_rest_impact() to compare the components with wins and spread covers.

Examples

games <- subset(nfl_schedules_sample, game_id == "2024_02_SEA_NE")
advantage <- calculate_schedule_advantage(games)
advantage[, c("game_id", "rest_points", "travel_points",
              "time_zone_points", "schedule_advantage")]
#> # A tibble: 1 x 5
#>   game_id        rest_points travel_points time_zone_points schedule_advantage
#>   <chr>                <dbl>         <dbl>            <dbl>              <dbl>
#> 1 2024_02_SEA_NE           0          2.49             1.05               3.54
